title: Search Superiority Recollection Familiarity
description: EEG and eye-tracking dataset from 30 participants who searched for objects in real-world scenes or intentionally memorized objects in other scenes, then completed a surprise recognition memory test. The study asks whether the search superiority effect reflects purely stronger memory or also qualitative differences in recollection versus familiarity. The data include FN400 and LPC ERP components, remember-know judgments, and receiver operating characteristics. Behavioral data are split into encoding and memory testing phases.
methods_description: Participants performed a visual search task on some scenes and an intentional memorization task on others while EEG and eye movements were recorded. A surprise recognition memory test with remember-know judgments followed. Behavioral data are provided separately for encoding (Encode_beh) and testing (Test_beh).
